question: Which floating fern damages aquatic ecosystems by outgrowing and replacing native plants that provide food and habitat for native animals and water flow?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Giant Salvinia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **One of the most troublesome water plants in Texas **right now is **giant Salvinia (Salvinia molesta)**, a floating fern from southern Brazil. By outgrowing and displacing native plants that provide food and habitat for local animals and waterfowl, it** harms aquatic ecosystems.**
 
• **Salvinia molesta is an aquatic fern** that is indigenous to south-eastern Brazil. It is also known as gigantic Salvinia or Kariba weed since it contaminated a sizable area of **Lake Kariba between Zimbabwe and Zambia.**
 
• **Salvinia's characteristics include Small, floaters with branching**, creeping stems that have hairs on the papillae of the leaf surfaces but **no true roots.**
 
• The** leaves are arranged in trimerous whorls, **with one leaf being finely divided, petiolate, rootlike, and pendant, while the other two are green, sessile or short-petioled, flat, **whole, and floating. **​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A** species of aquatic floating fern called Salvinia minima** develops on the surface of still waters. It is frequently known to as water spangles or common salvinia. Salvinia minima was brought to the United States in the 1920s and 1930s from its native regions of **South America, Mesoamerica, and the West Indies.**
 
• A** native of Europe, Africa, and Asia, Osmunda regalis**, often known as the royal fern, grows in wooded bogs and along the sides of streams. Due to the appearance of its fertile fronds, the species is occasionally referred to as a** blossoming fern.**
 
• The fern species **Azolla pinnata is also referred to as mosquito fern**, feathered mosquito fern, and water velvet. It is indigenous to large portions of** Africa, Asia, and Australia. **
